title: The Lady Detectives (BBC Radio)
paragraphs: Four-part BBC Radio 4 anthology dramatizing early female-detective fiction, adapted by Roger Danes and produced by Patrick Rayner. Frozen GRH set contains the complete run.
GRH documents the program through BBC Radio 4 January 2005 run (January 3, 2005 to January 24, 2005) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Patrick Rayner (producer on 4 recordings), Roger Danes (radio adaptor on 4 recordings), Gayanne Potter (performer on 3 recordings), Abigail Docherty (performer on 2 recordings), Crawford Logan (performer on 2 recordings), Eileen McCallum (performer on 2 recordings), and Paul Young (performer on 2 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include women detectives in early crime fiction, Victorian and Edwardian detective fiction, inheritance, wills and financial motive, jewel theft and society crime, and Scottish law and the not-proven verdict.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including BBC Radio 4 The Lady Detectives run and BBC revival of early female detective fiction.
plain_text:
Four-part BBC Radio 4 anthology dramatizing early female-detective fiction, adapted by Roger Danes and produced by Patrick Rayner. Frozen GRH set contains the complete run.

GRH documents the program through BBC Radio 4 January 2005 run (January 3, 2005 to January 24, 2005) on BBC Radio 4.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Patrick Rayner (producer on 4 recordings), Roger Danes (radio adaptor on 4 recordings), Gayanne Potter (performer on 3 recordings), Abigail Docherty (performer on 2 recordings), Crawford Logan (performer on 2 recordings), Eileen McCallum (performer on 2 recordings), and Paul Young (performer on 2 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include women detectives in early crime fiction, Victorian and Edwardian detective fiction, inheritance, wills and financial motive, jewel theft and society crime, and Scottish law and the not-proven verdict.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including BBC Radio 4 The Lady Detectives run and BBC revival of early female detective fiction.
